title: The body is a collective intelligence, so behavioural tools should beat micromanagement

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The body is a collective intelligence, so behavioural tools should beat micromanagement

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin's central hypothesis is that the body is a collective intelligence behaving in anatomical, physiological and transcriptional spaces, so behavioural-science tools developed to collaborate with complex systems should provide therapeutic advantages over biochemical micromanagement of molecular components.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Introduction › BOX 1

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The central hypothesis is that the body is a collective intelligence behaving in anatomical, physiological, and transcriptional spaces [13]. Thus, behavioral science tools developed to collaborate with complex systems should provide therapeutic advantages over biochemical micromanagement.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Introduction › BOX 1”. Scope: Human and animal bodies; biomedical and bioengineering interventions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-02: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction is testable after defining intervention classes and outcomes. Current public clinical and preclinical data do not provide controlled head-to-head tests broad enough to resolve the central claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In matched disease models, compare interventions designed as training or high-level state cues against molecular micromanagement for efficacy, durability, adverse effects and complexity. Consistent superiority of behavioural-style protocols would support the therapeutic prediction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Therapeutic advantage requires prospective comparative evidence.

Existing studies are not matched on indication and endpoint.

Collective intelligence does not define one intervention class.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.15
data existence: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The therapeutic prediction can be stated as a comparison of outcomes, so it is testable in principle. Existing papers report individual bioelectric or training interventions, but they are not a dataset that contrasts those approaches with biochemical micromanagement across indications. Settling the general claim requires that comparative evidence, which is not publicly available.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Match interventions that set a tissue-level target, using stimuli, training, or physiological setpoints, against interventions that manipulate the same outcome by editing individual molecular parts, and compare effect size, durability, and off-target cost. A consistent advantage for the first class would support the therapeutic claim; no advantage would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Published case studies use incommensurable endpoints and are mostly preclinical.

No public trial or experimental archive is structured as behavior-level versus molecular micromanagement.

Collective intelligence in anatomical space is not a covariate in clinical outcome datasets.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.25
analysis feasibility: 0.25
operationalizability: 0.6
discriminating power: 0.35
